question: Ain-i Akbari, a document on life of Mughal ruler Akbar does not contain information about ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ancestors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ain-i Akbari does not contain** information about Akbar's "**Ancestors**".
 
• The** Ain-i Akbari is the third volume of the Akbarnama, written by Abul Fazl, one of the Nine Gems (Navratnas) in Akbar's court.**
 
• This document offers a detailed account of **Akbar's reign, including his administration, the state's revenues, and the army.**
 
• However, it does not offer detailed information about his ancestors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The Akbarnama, in its first volume, does discuss Akbar's ancestors, but the **Ain-i Akbari, being the third volume, focuses more on Akbar's own reign and governance, not his lineage.**
 
• Th**e Ain-i Akbari is a five-part book which deals with the court, military establishment, the religions of the empire, the imperial administration, and the social conditions of the empire, among other aspects. It does not delve into the history of Akbar's ancestors.**
 
• The **focus of the Ain-i Akbari is more empirical and administrative, providing intricate details about Akbar's administration, army, and revenue collection.**
 
• **It provides detailed and accurate statistical data about various aspects of Mughal governance.**
 
• The Ain-i Akbari, unlike some other historical documents, isn't a genealogical record or a family history.
 
• **Its primary purpose was to document the empire under Akbar's reign.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Explanation
 
 
 
 

 Revenues
 
 
The Ain-i Akbari provides a detailed account of the state's revenues.

 
It describes the Mughal fiscal system, detailing the revenue of each province (subah), district, and village.

 
 
 

 Army
 
 
The Ain-i Akbari presents a detailed picture of the Mughal army, its structure, and its organization.

 
It provides an account of the rank and file in the Mughal military.

 
 
 

 Administration
 
 
The Ain-i Akbari provides comprehensive details about Akbar's administration, including the civil, judicial, and military administrations.

 
It details the bureaucratic structure and various administrative practices of the Mughal Empire under Akbar.
